title: Brooklyn Bridge Park, Pier 1
text: The postcard view: up to {max} landmarks from the pier, {median} from a typical spot, with the Brooklyn Bridge close by and the Statue of Liberty down the harbor.

title: Mount Olivet Cemetery
text: The most landmarks visible from any public spot in the model: {n} of 16, from a hillside about {elev} feet above sea level in Maspeth. Only the {missing} is out of sight. From a typical spot in the cemetery, {median}.

title: Highland Park
text: The glaciers left a ridge along the Brooklyn–Queens border. From the park's hilltop, west of the old Ridgewood Reservoir, {n} of the 16 are in view across the flats below. Much of the park is wooded and sees none.

title: Times Square
text: In the middle of the skyline, you can't see it: from {zero_share} of the bowtie's plazas, none of the 16 is visible. Only a narrow strip at the north end, by the TKTS steps, catches the Empire State Building.

title: Washington Square
text: Fifth Avenue starts at the arch and runs straight at the Empire State Building, {esb_mi} miles north. On the map, much of the avenue lights up like a beam.

title: Manhattanhenge on 42nd Street
text: Twice a year the setting sun lines up with the cross streets. On the map's Manhattanhenge evening, this stretch of 42nd Street sees the sun low over New Jersey, within about {sun_mins} minutes of sunset.

title: Brooklyn Heights Promenade at sunset
text: A view the city's zoning protects by law. Around the equinoxes you can watch the sun sink low over the harbor from the whole walk. In June, from nearly all of it, the sun drops behind the Financial District's towers 20 to 40 minutes or more before sunset.

title: Sunrise at Rockaway Beach
text: In winter the sun comes up out of the Atlantic, with nothing in the way: you see it within about {sun_mins} minutes of sunrise.

title: Sunset Park
text: Near the top of one of Brooklyn's high points, about {elev} feet up: up to {max} landmarks across the harbor and the city, {median} from a typical spot in the park.

title: Jamaica Bay Wildlife Refuge
text: On the West Pond trail the marsh opens onto the skyline: up to {max} landmarks, {median} from a typical spot on the loop, out to the {far_name}, {far_mi} miles away.

title: Wards Island
text: Some of Manhattan's widest views are off the main island: up to {max} landmarks here, {median} from a typical spot, with the Hell Gate Bridge's arch next door.

title: Alice Austen House
text: Staten Island's front porch on the Narrows: up to {max} landmarks, {median} from a typical spot, from the Verrazzano to the Midtown towers.

title: Ferry Point Park
text: The Bronx sees few of these landmarks on average, but this park near where the East River opens into Long Island Sound takes in up to {max} from its best spot ({median} from a typical one).

title: Calvary Cemetery
text: Midtown rising behind the headstones, a view familiar from the movies: up to {max} landmarks, {median} from a typical spot.

title: Domino Park
text: From the old sugar refinery's waterfront, up to {max} landmarks across the East River, {median} from a typical spot.

title: The Empire State's longest reach
text: The farthest public ground in the city that still sees the Empire State Building: Huguenot Avenue on Staten Island's South Shore, {esb_mi} miles away. The line of sight clears the ground in between by less than a metre, so this is the very edge of what's possible, and within the model's margin of error.
